subject: biology
title: Required practical: effect of pH on amylase
key_idea: In this practical, amylase is mixed with starch at different pH values. Drops of the mixture are tested with iodine every 30 seconds. The time taken for the starch to disappear shows how well the enzyme works at each pH.

blocks.text: Amylase is an enzyme that breaks down starch. This practical finds how pH changes the rate at which it does so.

rows: The pH, set using buffer solutions
The time taken for all the starch to be digested
Volume and concentration of starch, amylase and buffer. Temperature, kept constant in a water bath or with an electric heater.

items: Iodine solution is orange or brown.
If starch is present, it turns blue-black.
If there is no starch, it stays orange or brown.
Change the pH. Keep everything else the same.
Measure the time taken until the iodine stays orange or brown.
Blue-black means starch is still present.

blocks.text: This is a continuous sampling method. You test the same mixture again and again until the starch has gone.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of the amylase and pH practical in order.
steps: Put a drop of iodine solution into each well of a spotting tile
Mix amylase, starch and a buffer of one pH in a test tube and start the timer
Every 30 seconds, remove a drop of the mixture and add it to a well of iodine
Stop when the iodine stays orange or brown

items.text: Put one drop of iodine solution into each well of a spotting tile.
In a test tube in a water bath, mix amylase solution, starch solution and a buffer solution of one pH. Start the timer.
Every 30 seconds, use a pipette to move one drop of the mixture into a new well of iodine.
Blue-black means starch is still present. Continue until the iodine stays orange or brown.
Write down the time taken for all the starch to be digested.
Do the same at each pH, using the same volumes and concentrations and the same temperature.

items: Test a drop every 30 seconds, using a new well each time.
Use a buffer to set the pH. Use a water bath to keep the temperature constant.
Repeat at different pH values.

blocks.text: A shorter time means the enzyme is working faster. The best pH is the one with the shortest time.

blocks.label: Rate of reaction
where: time taken for the starch to be digested, in s

diagram.alt: A bell-shaped curve. The rate of amylase reaction rises as pH increases from acidic, peaks near pH 7, then falls again at higher pH.

items: At the optimum pH the starch is digested in the shortest time.
Above or below the optimum the active site changes shape and the rate falls.
At extreme pH values the enzyme is denatured and the starch is not broken down.
Shortest time means the fastest rate.
The optimum pH of amylase is close to 7.
To find the optimum more precisely, test more pH values close to it.

blocks.text: Exam questions ask how to make the results more accurate and how to check the optimum.

checks.q: How can you tell that all the starch has been digested?
checks.a: The iodine solution stays orange or brown, and does not turn blue-black.

checks.q: What is the independent variable in the investigation?
checks.a: The pH of the amylase solution (the buffer).

checks.q: Give two variables that must be controlled.
checks.a: Any two from: temperature; volume of starch, amylase or buffer; concentration of starch or amylase.

worked_example.question:
Amylase is an enzyme which breaks down starch.

Describe a method to investigate the effect of pH on the rate of starch breakdown by amylase.
answer_points: Add iodine solution to a spotting tile.
Use a measuring cylinder to add amylase solution, pH solution and starch solution together, and start the timer.
Use a pipette to remove a drop of the mixture at regular intervals, for example every 30 seconds, and add it to the iodine solution.
If starch is present, the mixture and iodine solution turn blue-black.
Continue until the iodine solution and the mixture remain yellow, orange or brown. Record the time taken.
Repeat at different pH values and compare the times at each pH.
Control variables: the volume and concentration of the starch, amylase and pH solutions, and the temperature.
worked_example.tip: This is a levelled answer. A valid method with the key steps in a logical order, and control variables named for a pH investigation, reaches the top level of 5 to 6 marks.

worked_example.question:
As apples ripen, enzymes convert starch into sugars.

Devise a method to find the optimum pH of an enzyme that breaks down starch.

You may use standard laboratory equipment and the solutions listed in the box.

starch solution   enzyme solution   iodine solution   a range of pH solutions
answer_points: Mix starch, enzyme and pH solution.
Use iodine to test for starch.
With iodine solution, blue-black means starch is present and orange or brown means no starch is present.
Control one variable, for example concentration, volume or temperature.
worked_example.tip: Any four points score one mark each. All three solutions must be used. Adding the iodine to a spotting tile is accepted.

worked_example.question:
Lipase is an enzyme produced in the human digestive system. It breaks down lipids.

Phenolphthalein is an indicator that turns pink in an alkaline solution of pH 10.

When lipase breaks down lipids, the indicator goes colourless.

A group of students investigate how temperature affects the enzymes that break down lipids found in milk.

Describe an experiment that the students could use to investigate the effect of temperature on the breakdown of the lipids found in milk.

In your description include:
- how the independent variable could be changed
- the observations that should be made
- two variables that need to be controlled.
answer_points: Independent variable (maximum 2): change the temperature, and say how it is maintained or changed, for example a water bath or Bunsen burner.
Observations (maximum 2): record the time it takes for the indicator to change colour, to colourless, and use a stop clock.
Controlled variables (maximum 2): volume or mass of milk, concentration of enzyme, volume or mass of enzyme, type of milk.
worked_example.tip: Marks are given in three groups. In this question temperature is the variable you change, so it cannot also be a controlled variable. "Amount" is ignored, so give a volume or a mass. For a pH investigation the plan is the same, but you change the pH and keep the temperature constant.
